habitat: Single birds or scattered individuals at the waterside on quiet rivers, lakes, dams and floodplains, or walking on floating vegetation. It is not secretive.
summary: A common resident. Identified by red legs and a bright yellow bill. Newman does not name the body colour in the text. The immature is a duller version of the adult, with a dark bill and dark legs. The call is an explosive harsh rr-rr-rr ending in a resonant croak, and it also clucks. Newman’s page uses Amaurornis flavirostra. This list keeps Zapornia flavirostra. The Kemp name Black Crake and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Rail is larger, with a long red bill. Black Crake has a short bright yellow bill and red legs.
